name: The Transfiguration of the Lord
history: Christ took Peter, James and John up a high mountain, by tradition Mount Tabor, and was transfigured before them: His face shone like the sun and His clothes became white as light. Moses and Elijah spoke with Him of His coming death, and the Father’s voice said, This is my beloved Son; listen to Him.
life: All three synoptic Gospels tell of the Transfiguration, and Saint Peter recalls it in his second letter: we were eyewitnesses of His majesty, when we were with Him on the holy mountain. It came soon after Christ first foretold His Passion, and the Fathers saw in it a gift to strengthen the apostles for the scandal of the cross. Moses and Elijah stand for the Law and the Prophets, both fulfilled in Him. Peter, not knowing what he said, wanted to build three tents and stay. The feast was kept in the East from early centuries. In 1457 Pope Callixtus III extended it to the whole Western Church, in thanksgiving for the relief of Belgrade the year before, news of which had reached Rome on 6 August.
prayerTo: Lord Jesus, transfigured on the mountain, you showed your friends your glory before they saw you suffer. When my faith is tested by darkness and pain, let me remember the light of your face. Help me to listen to you, as the Father commands, and bring me at last to see you as you are. Amen.
penance: Climb a hill or find a high place today if you can, and pray there; otherwise read Matthew 17:1–9 slowly and in silence.
meditation: It is good for us to be here, said Peter. Jesus led them back down the mountain. Where is He asking you to carry the light of prayer into ordinary work today?
prayer: O God, Who in the glorious Transfiguration of Your only-begotten Son strengthened the mysteries of faith by the testimony of the fathers, and, by the voice coming down in a shining cloud, miraculously betokened the complete adoption of Your children, mercifully grant that we be made co-heirs with that King of glory, and sharers in that same glory. Through the same Christ our Lord…
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
